_about: The one place that says which courses exist and which must come first. The build reads it to make the course map in every guide's side menu, the 'Comes after' line on each welcome screen, the next-course buttons at the end of a course, and the landing page. 'lessons' is the file with the course's LESSONS; 'tagline' and 'about' are for page titles and search results (about: under 160 characters). 'pain' is the everyday problem the course fixes, for the landing page. 'needs' lists the courses that must be finished first (only the direct ones: Git needs Shell 2, and Shell 2 already needs Shell). A course whose 'folder' is null is planned, not built: it shows as 'coming later'. 'store' is the browser storage key the guide keeps its progress under. 'recap' is the file with its "What I've learnt" words, shown when someone asks what a course is about on the course map. Card fields (cmd, blurb, button, colour) are for the landing page. tests/curriculum.mjs checks this file.
_site: The address the site is published at, like https://example.org/jelly/ (with the closing slash). With it set, the build writes canonical links, sitemap.xml and robots.txt for search engines. null leaves them out.

courses.pain: A tutorial says “open a terminal”, and you freeze.
courses.about: A free, interactive command line course for curious kids. Learn ls, cd, cat, mv and more in a safe pretend terminal in your browser. Nothing to install.
courses.title: Jelly Shell
courses.blurb: Boss your computer around with tiny words. Move around folders, read and copy files, and rescue the gerbil.

courses.pain: It says Permission denied, and you have no idea why.
courses.about: Free interactive course: users, file permissions, chmod, sudo, writing your own commands, grep and pipes, in a safe pretend terminal in your browser.
courses.title: Jelly Shell 2
courses.blurb: Who's in charge? Users, groups and file locks. Write your own commands, borrow the boss's power, and use pipes to find out who ate the cookies.

courses.pain: A week of work is gone, and there is no way back.
courses.about: Learn git the friendly way: save snapshots, undo mistakes, and back your code up to GitHub. Free, interactive, in a safe pretend terminal in your browser.
courses.title: Jelly Git
courses.blurb: Never lose your code again. Save snapshots, undo mistakes and work with other people without stepping on their changes.

courses.pain: You want to learn hacking, the legal way.
courses.about: Same skills, different permission. Break into a pretend computer, fix the hole, then try again. A free, safe first step into cyber security.
courses.title: Jelly Security 1
courses.blurb: Same skills, different permission. Break into a pretend computer, fix the hole, then try again. Three missions.

courses.pain: You want your own website, on the real internet.
courses.tagline: how websites work, and make your own
courses.about: Write your own web page in HTML and CSS, follow it across the internet (DNS, HTTP, HTTPS), then publish it free with GitHub Pages. Free and in your browser.
courses.title: Jelly Web
courses.blurb: Write your own web page, find out how it crosses the planet in under a second, then put it on the internet with GitHub Pages.

courses.title: Jelly Security 2
courses.blurb: Attack and defend a pretend website: passwords, lookalike addresses, secret pages and who else can see your messages.

courses.title: Jelly Think 1
courses.blurb: Meet Wobble, a jelly robot that does exactly what you say and nothing more. Give it orders in real JavaScript, hunt the bugs, and learn to think like a programmer.

courses.title: Jelly Server
courses.blurb: Make your website answer back. Write a pretend server in real JavaScript: a guestbook that shows everyone's messages.

courses.title: Jelly Think 2
courses.blurb: What computers can't do, what takes forever, what goes wrong when two things happen at once, and what AI really is. Then: what you shouldn't build.

courses.title: Jelly Storage
courses.blurb: Your guestbook forgets everything when the server restarts. Teach it to remember, with files and JSON.

courses.title: Jelly SQL
courses.blurb: Ask a database questions. Find every message from one person, count them, and join tables together.
